transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. What brings you here today?

Well, I guess the main thing is I just can’t seem to keep my mind on one thing anymore, and it’s starting to mess me up at work. I’m in the warehouse, so there’s always noise and movement, you know—beepers going off, forklift alarms, somebody shifting a pallet or calling out—and every little thing just pulls me right off what I’m doing.

Like if I’m counting inventory, I’ll be on a number and then a beeper goes off, and suddenly I’m looking over there, and when I come back I’m not sure where I was. Then later I realize I put the wrong numbers in. It’s embarrassing, honestly, because I know how to do my job. I’ve done this kind of work a long time. But lately it’s like my mind just jumps to whatever is happening around me, and I can’t hold the count in my head long enough to finish it right.
Do you find yourself getting distracted like this in other places too, like at home or when you're out with friends, or does it only happen at work?

It’s mostly at work that I really notice it, because that’s where it actually causes a problem I can point to. Like in the warehouse, if I’m counting inventory or trying to keep track of numbers, and then a beeper goes off or a forklift alarm starts up, or someone moves a pallet nearby, my attention just snaps over there. Then when I turn back, I’ve lost the count, and I’ll think I remember where I was, but later I find out I put the wrong number in.

At home or with friends, it’s harder to say because there isn’t that same kind of counting or inventory where I can see the mistake afterward. I mean, I might get pulled off by things, but at work it’s obvious because the numbers come out wrong, and that’s what’s bothering me. It’s not that I don’t know how to do the work—I do. It’s just like my mind won’t stay on the one thing long enough when there’s noise or movement around me.
Do you ever feel restless, fidgety, or like you can’t sit still for very long? Or find yourself acting without thinking, like interrupting others or starting new tasks before finishing old ones?

Yeah… not so much like I’m bouncing my leg nonstop or physically can’t stay in a chair, but I have been kind of… taking on a lot. More than I usually would.

At work, for example, I started getting really focused on safety stuff. Like, I’ll notice some little thing with how pallets are stacked or where people are walking, and then suddenly I’m making notes about it, and then that turns into a whole safety-improvement idea. I’ve been bringing up extra projects, making lists of what should be changed, who should do what, what signs we need, how the flow should be better—like I’m running some big operation instead of just doing my regular job.

And outside work too, I’ve been signing up for more art workshops than I normally would. Usually I might do one here or there, but lately I’m looking at schedules, trying to fit in multiple classes, making plans for supplies, times, what I’m going to make. I’ll write it all out like it’s a production schedule.

So I don’t know if that’s the same as acting without thinking, exactly, but I do feel like I keep starting more things and organizing more things than I normally take on.
Have you noticed that you’ve been more active than usual, like moving around more, starting a lot of projects, or feeling like you need to keep going without slowing down?

Yeah, actually… that part I have noticed. After my shifts, I used to come home and be done. Like, I’d get in, maybe eat something, sit on the couch, and my body would feel like, okay, that’s enough for today. The warehouse work is physical, so being tired after made sense.

But lately I come home and I’m still kind of… buzzing. Not in a good relaxed way, more like I can’t just sit there. I’ll tell myself I’m going to rest, and then I’m up opening cabinets, pulling everything out, deciding the whole kitchen cabinet needs to be reorganized right then. Or I’ll go into the garage and start sorting bins—like tools in one pile, old stuff in another, containers stacked a certain way—and suddenly it’s been an hour or two.

It’s not even always something that really needed doing that minute. It just feels uncomfortable to sit on the couch and do nothing. Like my body is tired from work, but something in me is still pushing, like I have to keep going or use up all this energy somehow.
Have you noticed any period of time in which you felt unusually energetic, excited, or irritable — like you didn’t need as much sleep, or like you could take on more than usual without getting tired?

Yeah… there have been days like that. Not every single day, but enough that I’ve noticed it, and my husband definitely notices it.

Some days I wake up or get going and I’m just… almost too upbeat, if that makes sense. Like I’m looking around the house thinking, okay, I can fix this, I can reorganize that, I can finally solve the mess in the garage, and then I’m also thinking about things at work, like safety changes or better ways to set things up there. It feels like I can take on the whole house and the workplace before dinner, like it all seems possible and urgent at the same time.

But then it can flip into me being really sharp with people. Like if my husband says something reasonable, like, “Do you really need to do that right now?” or “Maybe slow down,” I’ll snap at him over some tiny thing. In the moment it feels like he’s blocking me or criticizing the plan, and I get irritated fast. Then afterward I’m like… why did I react that strongly? It was such a small comment.

This addition reflects new symptoms that extend beyond inattention and include psychomotor activation and goal-directed behavior that could be indicative of bipolar disorder rather than ADHD or major depressive disorder alone.
